principles.statement: Every agent's model and tool usage is metered per day and per tool in a durable ledger — usage is a counted fact, never an estimate.
principles.rationale: The usage ledger keys buckets by (agent, day, tool) and increments on every call, refused or not: refusals are metering events too, and the gate refuses with a real structured error when the daily budget is exhausted.

principles.statement: A budget gate must refuse with real, actionable structure — the caller receives an explicit McpResult error naming the limit — never a silent empty result or a fabricated partial answer.
principles.rationale: The gate's refusal is itself a metered, logged event; 'no budget' and 'no answer' are different facts and the system says which one happened.

principles.statement: Metering exists to enable tuning decisions from real numbers — the ledger is the reference dataset for cost questions.
principles.rationale: Per-tool breakdown answers 'what does an agent actually spend on'; without the breakdown a budget is a guess enforced by a guess.

heuristics.name: Adding any new agent, tool, or model call path.
heuristics.description: Wire it through the metered call surface (McpCall -> ledger increment) in the same change; an unmetered path is a missing feature, not a shortcut.

heuristics.name: Investigating cost or budget questions.
heuristics.description: Read the ledger's per-agent/day/tool buckets; never reconstruct usage from memory or logs after the fact.

decision_rules.condition: An agent's daily usage reaches its budget.
decision_rules.action: Refuse further calls with a real structured limit error naming agent, day, and tool; still record the refused attempt in the ledger.
